stem: In the figure, \(\overline{AD}\) bisects angle \(BAC\), and point \(D\) lies on \(\overline{BC}\). Angle \(BAC\) measures \(50^{\circ}\), and the measure of angle \(ADC\) is \(24^{\circ}\) greater than the measure of angle \(ADB\). What is the measure, in degrees, of angle \(ACB\)?
solution: Each half of the bisected angle measures \(25^{\circ}\). Angle \(ADC\) is an exterior angle of triangle \(ABD\), so angle \(ADC = 25 + B\). Likewise angle \(ADB = 25 + C\).
The difference is \((25 + B) - (25 + C) = B - C = 24\).
Also \(B + C = 180 - 50 = 130\). Adding the two equations: \(2B = 154\), so \(B = 77\) and \(C = 130 - 77 = 53\).
verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert P['B'][1]==P['C'][1]==P['D'][1] and P['B'][0]<P['D'][0]<P['C'][0]
assert abs(ang('B','A','C')-50)<0.1 and abs(ang('B','A','D')-ang('D','A','C'))<0.1
assert abs((ang('A','D','C')-ang('A','D','B'))-24)<0.1
Bs,Cs=symbols('Bs Cs')
sol=solve([Eq(Bs+Cs,130),Eq((180-25-Cs)-(180-25-Bs),24)],[Bs,Cs])
ans=sol[Cs]
assert abs(ang('A','C','B')-ans)<0.1
assert Rational(spr_answers[0])==ans==53
